text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The cabinet decided to provide 500 million pounds ($150 million) as a first instalment to finance purchases of wheat from farmers, in the light of the way wheat deliveries have exceeded the target by 30 percent. The cabinet also approved a timetable for finishing off the Abu Tartour phosphate project, to develop it into a complex for chemical and mineral production so that it is eligible for offering to serious investors.
The cabinet also set August 1 as a the date for deciding which company should be awarded the contract for building the giant pumping station to feed the Toshka project.
Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif also said that the cabinet decided to allocate 70 million pounds to dig 85 wells along the Darb el-Arbaeen to reclaim 12,000 acres of land there.

- President Hosni Mubarak made a phone call to King Fahd of Saudi Arabia and they discussed a number of issues of mutual interest, bilateral, regional and international. Crown Prince Abdullah bin Abdul-Aziz ended his three-day visit.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said any talk about Jerusalem that violated the agreements signed and U.N. resolutions would have a negative effect on the "final status" talks.
- Presidential adviser Osama el-Baz had talks in Washington with Samuel Berger, President Bill Clinton's National Security adviser. They discussed Egypt's mediation efforts.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said protecting those on limited incomes was the priority concern of President Mubarak.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said that the voluntary early retirement scheme would start at 20 public-sector companies from July 1. Compensation will range from 12,000 to 35,000 pounds.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said it was too early to talk about any opening in the Middle East peace process, especially in the light of Israeli statements on Jerusalem.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will lay the foundation stone for the suspension bridge across the Suez Canal tomorrow. The bridge will cost 500 million pounds and Japan is financing 60 percent of the costs.
- The World Bank said in the next phase the Egyptian government would give priority to alleviating poverty.
- The public prosecutor's office is continuing its investigations into the complaint filed by Mubarak's sons against the Saudi-owned newspaper Asharq al-Awsat.
